intro.title: Conditional Classes
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple notification component that changes its appearance based on different message types. You'll learn how to conditionally apply CSS classes to React elements using JavaScript expressions. The main technologies involved are React JSX, JavaScript ternary operators, and template literals for string concatenation. By the end, you'll understand how to dynamically control styling based on component state or props.
intro.usecase: Conditional classes are essential for creating dynamic, responsive interfaces that react to user interactions and application state. In real-world applications, you'll use them to highlight active navigation items in dashboards, indicate form validation errors, toggle dark/light themes, or show loading states on buttons. For example, when a user selects a filter option in an e-commerce site, conditional classes visually distinguish the active filter from inactive ones. This pattern appears everywhere from social media platforms that mark unread notifications to project management tools that indicate task completion status through visual cues.
